title: Principality of Valona
capsule: The Principality of Valona (centred on modern Vlorë in Albania) was established around 1346 when the Serbian emperor Stefan Dušan granted the region to John Komnenos Asen, his brother-in-law, who held the Byzantine title of Despot. After Dušan's death in 1355 the principality became effectively independent, maintaining profitable trade relations with Venice and Ragusa; John adopted Byzantine court customs and signed his documents in Greek. He died of plague in 1363, and after his widow ruled briefly, control passed through marriage to the Muzaka and then to the Balsha dynasty—Balsha II was killed at the Battle of Savra in 1385—before the Ottomans completed their conquest in 1417.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The principality's core territory—the hinterland of Vlorë, Fier, and Berat—is described in Venetian and Serbian sources, but precise borders fluctuated considerably as rival Albanian lords competed for control.
